title: Vesta raises $30M to bring swarms of agents to mortgage lenders
key_facts: Vesta, an AI-native software startup that helps lenders originate mortgages, raised a $30 million round led by Conversion Capital, announced Thursday 8 Oct 2026.
Customers Pennymac and New American Funding invested, with Citi Ventures and Andreessen Horowitz; total raised is $85 million.
CEO Mike Yu says revenue is up 12x year over year and the company has under 5% market share.
Closing a US mortgage takes about 40 days and costs around $11,000 per loan, mostly human labor.
Lenders often start an agent with a person approving its work, then let it handle a share of loans alone; some use Vesta agents to make underwriting decisions.
Companies remain responsible for underwriting decisions and every action and its reasoning is recorded for audit.
Competitors include ICE Mortgage Technology and Xpanse.
